battle.name: 第二次印巴戰爭
battle.theater: 克什米爾與旁遮普前線
battle.brief: 第二次印巴戰爭（1965年）爆發於克什米爾與旁遮普，雙方投入大量機械化兵團。巴基斯坦陸軍在這場衝突中使用了美製M4A1雪曼坦克，該坦克早於1942年服役，並在戰爭中提供重要裝甲支援。

kit.name: M4A1雪曼坦克
kit.history: M4A1雪曼坦克是二戰期間美國主力中型坦克，後來退役或轉讓至盟友，1965年巴基斯坦軍隊在印巴戰爭中將其作為裝甲突擊骨幹使用。

countries: 1965年第二次印巴戰爭的主要交據國是印度與巴基斯坦。巴基斯坦由西巴基斯坦與東巴基斯坦兩個軍區動員，主要攻勢放在西北邊境；印度則以西部與北部指揮部集中主力，防守蘇萊河、傑赫勒姆河、奇納布河沿線，以及通往斯利那加的公路和鐵路。拉合爾、錫亞爾科特、傑爾姆、帕坦科特、古爾普爾與卡爾吉爾是主要戰區，據點、鐵路和縱深道路把它們連接起來。蘇聯不是交戰國，而是派遣特使並主持塔什干會談；英國、美國及部分英聯邦國家提供外交、訓練或後勤協助，沒有以共同部隊投入戰場。因此，戰爭由兩條互相牽動的戰線組成：旁遮普平原會戰決定邊境突破能否維持，卡爾吉爾山地戰決定入境武力能否占據可防守的高地。
countriesEn: The principal belligerents in the 1965 Second Indo-Pakistani War were India and Pakistan. Pakistan mobilized through its West Pakistan and East Pakistan commands, placing its principal offensive on the northwestern frontier. India concentrated its main strength under Western and Northern Command to defend the Sutlej, Jhelum, and Chenab lines and the roads and railways leading to Srinagar. Lahore, Sialkot, Jammu, Pathankot, Gulpur, and Kargil formed the principal battlefields, linked by fortified positions, railways, and roads extending into the interior. The Soviet Union was not a belligerent; it sent an emissary and hosted the Tashkent talks. Britain, the United States, and several Commonwealth countries provided diplomatic, training, or logistical assistance but did not commit joint forces. The war therefore comprised two interconnected fronts: the battles of the Punjab plains determined whether a border breach could be sustained, while the mountain fighting at Kargil determined whether the infiltrating force could hold defensible heights.
people: 印度的政治與最高軍事決策由總理拉爾・巴哈杜爾・夏斯特里、國防部長亞什旺特勞・查萬和陸軍參謀長卡里亞帕元帥共同掌握。西部指揮部由喬杜里中將指揮，負責旁遮普與查莫克方向；北部指揮部由卡爾拉中將指揮，負責卡西姆山區。拉傑恩德拉辛吉中將率領第十五兵團，魯德拉少將指揮第一裝甲師，阿胡瓦利亞少將指揮第八山地師，使拉合爾反擊、錫亞爾科特裝甲戰和卡爾吉爾攻勢能由不同指揮鏈調度。巴基斯坦方面，總統阿尤布・汗決定向北進攻的戰略框架，武裝部隊參謀長穆罕默德・穆薩負責軍隊部署；阿克塔爾・阿卜杜勒・拉赫曼中將負責東巴基斯坦軍務，阿布拉爾・侯賽因少將指揮古吉拉尼瓦拉的第一兵團，艾尼斯・艾哈邁德少將則指揮錫亞爾科特方向的第十五步兵師。蘇聯總理柯西金後來以中立調解者身分促成塔什干協議，但沒有替任何一方提供戰場指揮。
peopleEn: India's political and top-level military decisions rested jointly with Prime Minister Lal Bahadur Shastri, Defence Minister Y. B. Chavan, and Army Chief of Staff Field Marshal K. M. Cariappa. Lieutenant General J. N. Chaudhuri commanded Western Command, which covered the Punjab and Chamb directions, while Lieutenant General G. S. Kalra commanded Northern Command in the Kashmir area. Lieutenant General Rajendrasinhji led XV Corps, Major General A. A. Rudra commanded the 1st Armoured Division, and Major General M. S. Ahluwalia commanded the 8th Mountain Division, giving separate command chains to the Lahore counteroffensive, the armoured battle at Sialkot, and the Kargil offensive. On the Pakistani side, President Ayub Khan determined the strategic framework for the northern offensive, while Chief of Army Staff General Muhammad Musa directed deployment. Lieutenant General Akhtar Abdur Rahman handled military affairs in East Pakistan, Major General Abrar Hussain commanded I Corps at Gujranwala, and Major General Anis Ahmad led the 15th Infantry Division in the Sialkot sector. Soviet Premier Aleksei Kosygin later acted as a neutral mediator at Tashkent but did not exercise battlefield command for either side.
kits: 雙方作戰裝備的核心都是第二次世界大戰時期形成體系的坦克、火砲與螺旋槳飛機。印度與巴基斯坦都使用美製M47及M48巴頓戰車、謝爾曼坦克和中國製59式戰車；印度另有英製百夫長、法製AMX-13與少量76毫米M18自走砲，巴基斯坦則以M47、M48、謝爾曼及59式構成主要裝甲力量。火炮包括英製四點五英吋野戰砲、二十五磅砲，以及美製105毫米M1A1或D1榴彈砲；步兵單位配備120毫米迫擊砲、三點七英吋反戰車砲和106毫米M40無後坐力砲，機槍則有維克斯型與英國製斯特林式。印度空軍在此役使用米格21FL魚床C、米格7、神秘IV、獵鷹、堪培拉及B-97圖夫式；巴基斯坦空軍使用幻象III、F-6、F-86F、獵鷹與堪培拉。F-6是米格19的仿製型，兩國空軍亦使用C-47道克納斯等運輸機。部署時還配屬野戰電話、無線電台、搶修車、工程器材、燃料桶、彈藥車與汽車修理工作組。以上型號在1965年以前均已服役，清單只表示可使用的裝備種類，不代表每個師都配足相同數量。
kitsEn: The core equipment of both sides consisted of Second World War-era tank, artillery, and propeller-aircraft systems. India and Pakistan both fielded the American M47 and M48 Patton tanks, Sherman tanks, and Chinese Type 59 tanks. India additionally operated the Centurion, French AMX-13, and a limited number of 76 mm M18 self-propelled guns, while Pakistan's principal armored strength came from the M47, M48, Sherman, and Type 59. Artillery included the British 4.5-inch field gun, the 25-pounder, and the American 105 mm M1A1 or D1 howitzer. Infantry formations had 120 mm mortars, 3.7-inch anti-tank guns, and 106 mm M40 recoilless rifles, with Vickers machine guns and British Sterling submachine guns in service. The Indian Air Force employed the MiG-21FL Fishbed-C, MiG-7, Mystère IV, Hunter, Canberra, and B-97 Toof. The Pakistan Air Force fielded the Mirage III, F-6, F-86F, Hunter, and Canberra. The F-6 was a Chinese-built derivative of the MiG-19, and both air forces also used C-47 Dakota transports. The field order of battle also included field telephones, radio sets, recovery vehicles, engineering equipment, fuel drums, ammunition trucks, and vehicle repair workshops. Every model listed had entered service before 1965; the inventory identifies available types, not identical quantities in every division.
tactics: 九月四日夜至五日，巴基斯坦空軍先行攻擊包括帕坦科特在內的空軍基地，並轟擊邊境公路、鐵路與若干橋梁；炮兵同時向傑爾姆、錫亞爾科特、拉合爾和卡西姆前線射擊。九月六日拂曉，標示「大打擊」的主要攻勢展開：第十五步兵師及裝甲部隊在錫亞爾科特越過蘇萊河，第十師投向傑爾姆，第十九師攻擊帕坦科特，第六裝甲師在拉合爾東側渡河，古爾普爾與傑赫勒姆方向則由步兵、炮兵和工程兵建立橋頭堡。印度沒有把所有裝甲部隊同時推向前線，而是以步兵、反戰車砲和逐線火力封住渡口，再由縱深部隊封閉突破口。錫亞爾科特方面，第一步兵師與第一裝甲師在多格諾奇、菲利奧拉一線反擊；密集的公路和河岸地形迫使巴基斯坦裝甲縱隊分批前進，使其無法迅速擴大突破口。拉合爾方面，第六裝甲師一度向鐵路與城市外圍推進，但第十五兵團以第十五步兵師、第五十四步兵師及第一裝甲師執行「阿杰」反擊，到九月十二日前後迫使巴基斯坦部隊撤回蘇萊河東側。帕坦科特跑道遭到嚴重破壞，但仍在印度控制之下；傑爾姆與古爾普爾的攻勢同樣沒有形成持續突破。卡西姆戰線最為激烈。九月七日開始，印度第八山地師和第十八步兵師在山炮、工兵與通信支援下展開「維杰」行動，黑岩與托洛林在九月八日前後失守，敵方據守的四八七五高點、三座山頭與老虎山則在九月十三日前後被印度控制；交通斷裂的巴基斯坦北方輕步兵與武裝入境者被逐個孤立，其餘零散陣地直至停火後才陸續撤除。巴基斯坦另在九月六日宣布單方面停火，希望聯合國介入，但印度認為攻勢仍在進行，沒有把該聲明視為有效中止作戰。九月十日，夏斯特里與阿尤布・汗在塔什干簽署協議，戰鬥在九月十一日全面停止。
tacticsEn: From the night of September 4 into September 5, the Pakistan Air Force struck air bases, including Pathankot, and attacked frontier roads, railways, and several bridges, while artillery opened fire against Jammu, Sialkot, Lahore, and the Kashmir front. At dawn on September 6, the main offensive designated Grand Slam began. The 15th Infantry Division and supporting armor crossed the Sutlej at Sialkot, the 10th Division was committed toward Jammu, the 19th Division attacked Pathankot, the 6th Armoured Division crossed east of Lahore, and infantry, artillery, and engineers established bridgeheads in the Gulpur and Jhelum sectors. India did not commit all armored formations simultaneously. Infantry, anti-tank guns, and fire along successive defensive lines confined the crossings, while reserves in depth closed the penetrations. At Sialkot, the 1st Infantry Division and 1st Armoured Division counterattacked around Dog Notch and Phillora. Constricted roads and riverbanks forced the Pakistani armored columns to advance in smaller groups, preventing a rapid expansion of the bridgehead. In the Lahore sector, the 6th Armoured Division advanced toward the railway and the approaches to the city, but XV Corps conducted Operation Ajay with the 15th Infantry Division, 54th Infantry Division, and 1st Armoured Division. By about September 12, those forces pushed the Pakistani units back east of the Sutlej. Pathankot's runway was badly damaged but remained under Indian control, and the attacks at Jammu and Gulpur likewise failed to produce sustained penetrations. The Kashmir front was the most intense. Beginning on September 7, the Indian 8th Mountain Division and 18th Infantry Division launched Operation Vijay with mountain artillery, engineers, and communications support. Black Rock and Tololing fell around September 8, while Point 4875, Three Pimple, and Tiger Hill came under Indian control around September 13. Pakistani Northern Light Infantry and armed infiltrators, isolated by the broken transport network, were defeated position by position, while scattered outposts withdrew only after the ceasefire. Pakistan had also declared a unilateral ceasefire on September 6 in the hope of United Nations intervention, but India regarded the continuing offensive as proof that the declaration had not halted operations. On September 10, Shastri and Ayub Khan signed the Tashkent agreement in Tashkent, and general fighting ceased on September 11.
data: 若以八月開始的邊境滲透與危機累積計算，戰事延續至九月下旬；九月六日至十一日的大規模正規會戰則不足一週。常見的戰後兵力概估把印度可用總量列為約三十個師、約一千二百輛戰車、約八百門火砲及九百架飛機；巴基斯坦約有十二至十三個師、二百五十輛戰車、三百門火砲及二百二十架飛機。這些數字包括預備與後續可調度部隊，並非全部同時位於前線。旁遮普補給主要利用德里至阿姆利則及昌迪加爾的鐵路、公路向前輸送；巴基斯坦則依賴拉合爾至瓦希拉巴德、錫亞爾科特等幹線及前進仓库。炮兵反覆射擊造成的主要後勤壓力是砲彈補充、車輛輪班與燃料前送，而不是單純增加射擊次數。季風帶來暴雨、泥濘和河水暴漲，使旁遮普道路阻塞，也限制卡爾吉爾山區的車輛通行。雙方對作戰傷亡、裝甲損失與空戰結果的統計口徑不同，當時亦無共同核驗的單一總表，因此不能把有爭議的精確傷亡數字視為定論。
dataEn: Measured from the beginning of the frontier infiltrations and accumulating crisis in August, the conflict continued into late September; the major conventional campaign from September 6 to September 11 lasted less than a week. Common postwar force estimates place India's available strength at approximately thirty divisions, 1,200 tanks, 800 artillery pieces, and 900 aircraft. Pakistan was assessed at roughly twelve to thirteen divisions, 250 tanks, 300 artillery pieces, and 220 aircraft. These figures include reserves and units available for later commitment and do not mean that every formation was simultaneously on the firing line. Punjab sustainment depended principally on the railways and roads from Delhi through Amritsar and Jalandhar, while Pakistan relied on the Lahore-Wazirabad and Sialkot rail corridors and forward depots. The principal logistics pressure created by repeated artillery fire was the replenishment of shells, rotation of transport vehicles, and forward delivery of fuel, rather than a simple increase in the number of firing rounds. The monsoon brought heavy rain, mud, and swollen rivers, obstructing roads in the Punjab and restricting vehicle movement in the Kargil mountains. The two sides used different methods of counting combat casualties, armored losses, and air-combat results, and no jointly verified single total existed. Conflicting precise casualty figures therefore cannot responsibly be treated as settled fact.
cause: 戰爭最深的根源仍是1947年停火後未經共同勘定與永久安排的卡西姆邊界，以及聯合國原會支持就此舉行全民投票的立場。巴基斯坦把1965年安排武裝人員越過停火線的行動稱為「直布羅陀行動」，目的之一是讓既定局勢發生變化並增加聯合國介入壓力；印度則把它視為掩盖正規部隊入侵的準備。雙方的軍事部署又形成連鎖反應：印度因情報與邊境徵候向旁遮普集中兵力，巴基斯坦將此解讀為印度即將進攻的證據，於是把更多裝甲、步兵與炮兵推向北線。巴基斯坦相信印度防衛存在可利用的空隙，也相信聯合國會在突破形成後迅速促成停火；印度則掌握空軍、裝甲預備隊與縱深步兵可在有限時間內投入反擊。八月情報、九月空襲與渡河準備證明巴基斯坦確有大規模作戰計畫，但雙方仍低估了政治象徵、外交承諾、裝甲受地形限制及後勤差異同時發揮的作用。
causeEn: The deepest cause of the war remained the Kashmir boundary created after the 1947 ceasefire, which had never been jointly surveyed or converted into a permanent arrangement, together with the original United Nations position that a plebiscite should determine the territory's future. Pakistan's 1965 deployment of armed personnel across the ceasefire line, known as Operation Gibraltar, was intended partly to alter the existing situation and increase pressure for United Nations involvement. India regarded it instead as cover for a regular invasion. Military deployments then produced a chain reaction. India concentrated troops in the Punjab after intelligence reports and frontier indications, while Pakistan interpreted that movement as evidence of an impending Indian attack and moved additional armor, infantry, and artillery northward. Pakistan believed Indian defenses contained exploitable gaps and expected the United Nations to arrange a rapid ceasefire once a breakthrough had been created. India, however, possessed air forces, armored reserves, and infantry in depth that could be committed to a counterattack within a limited time. Intelligence gathered during August and the air strikes and river preparations of September confirmed that Pakistan had a major operational plan, but both governments underestimated the combined effects of political symbolism, international commitments, terrain restrictions on armor, and differences in logistics.
impact: 在作戰層面，印度以有限縱深反擊封住了巴基斯坦在旁遮普的主要突破，並在卡爾吉爾重新控制主要高地；巴基斯坦則顯示封閉渡口、受限制道路與短暫空軍主動權不足以讓裝甲越過步兵和炮兵構成的正面阻力。空軍基地的疏散、跑道搶修與跑道旁分散駐機，使最初空襲未能長期阻止印度空軍作戰；前進彈藥與燃料倉庫遭空襲威脅，則凸顯部隊越過河流後仍依賴補給線的弱點。印度雖在戰場上取得多數可見成果，塔什干協議卻使主要邊境回到接近戰前狀態，巴基斯坦的入境武力未能占據永久陣地，印度也沒有藉此實現全面政治要求。蘇聯調解提高了其在南亞的外交影響力，英美則因戰爭可能失控而持續要求克制，儘管沒有直接投入部隊。雙方還得到另一項長期教訓：情報可能揭示敵方準備，卻不能代替對準備是否完整、補給能否持續及聯合國會如何反應的判斷。
impactEn: Operationally, India's limited counteroffensive contained Pakistan's principal penetrations in the Punjab and regained the principal heights at Kargil. Pakistan, in turn, demonstrated that closed river crossings, restricted roads, and brief air superiority could not carry armor through a front formed by infantry and artillery. The dispersal of aircraft, rapid runway repair, and revetted parking areas around Indian airfields prevented the initial strikes from keeping the Indian Air Force ineffective for long. Pakistani forward ammunition and fuel depots remained exposed to air attack, illustrating the vulnerability of an army even after it had crossed a river. Although India achieved most of the immediate battlefield gains, the Tashkent settlement returned the principal frontier to a condition close to that before the war. Pakistan's infiltrating force obtained no permanent territory, and India did not convert its military success into its full political demands. Soviet mediation increased Moscow's diplomatic influence in South Asia, while Britain and the United States continued to press for restraint because of the danger of uncontrolled escalation, although neither intervened directly. Both sides also learned that intelligence could reveal an opponent's preparations but could not replace judgments about whether those preparations were complete, whether supplies could be sustained, and how the United Nations would respond.
result: 九月十日，阿尤布・汗與夏斯特里在蘇聯主持下簽署塔什干聲明，宣布自九月十一日起停止敵對行動。主要安排是雙方部隊退回一九四七年八月一日以前的邊境態勢、撤出卡西姆地區的巴基斯坦武裝入境者、交換被俘人員並後送傷者。巴基斯坦先前的單方面停火聲明沒有取代這項雙邊協議。聯合國軍事觀察人員其後分階段核驗撤軍與停火線；印度占據的卡爾吉爾主要陣地沒有在停火時交還，巴基斯坦據點則依協議陸續撤除，俘獲人員在隨後數週內分批遣返，絕大多數回到原部隊。東邊界短暫越線形成的軍事優勢也在協議框架下撤回，拉德克萊夫線重新受到約束。就戰術結果而言，印度保住了卡西姆高地並迫使巴基斯坦越線部隊退出；就戰略與政治結果而言，雙方大致回到戰前態勢，巴基斯坦沒有取得永久邊境收益，印度沒有迫使聯合國接受全民投票，蘇聯則成為結束戰爭的直接調解者。零星射擊在停火後逐漸停止，俘獲、人員後送與實地撤軍則持續到後續數月。
resultEn: On September 10, Ayub Khan and Shastri signed the Tashkent Declaration under Soviet auspices and announced that hostilities would cease from September 11. Its principal provisions required the forces of both countries to return to the frontier conditions prevailing before August 1, 1947, required Pakistan to withdraw its armed infiltrators from Kashmir, and provided for the exchange of prisoners and the evacuation of the wounded. Pakistan's earlier unilateral cease-fire declaration did not replace the bilateral agreement. United Nations military observers subsequently verified the withdrawal and ceasefire arrangements in stages. India did not surrender the principal Kargil positions it held at the ceasefire, while Pakistani outposts were evacuated in accordance with the agreement. Prisoners of war were released in succeeding batches during the following weeks, and the great majority returned to their units. The temporary military advantage created by the brief crossing on the eastern frontier was also withdrawn within the agreement, and the Radcliffe Line was brought under its constraints once more. Tactically, India retained the Kargil heights and forced the Pakistani infiltrating formations out. Strategically and politically, both countries returned approximately to the prewar situation. Pakistan obtained no permanent territorial gain, India did not compel the United Nations to accept a plebiscite, and the Soviet Union became the direct mediator that ended the war. Sporadic firing diminished after the ceasefire, while prisoner exchanges, evacuation, and the physical implementation of withdrawals continued during the following months.
